Roof Ventilation and Condensation Control

We find out why a roof space is getting condensation and fix the cause, with internal lap vents for non-breathable bitumen felt and dry ridge ventilation where they are needed. Most jobs take 1 to 2 working days.

Find the Cause First

We look over the whole roof space to find out what's causing the condensation before anything is fitted. As roofers and insulation specialists, we know insulation and ventilation have to be balanced, and our own directly employed team does the work.

What Others Get Wrong

A common mistake is fitting vents without understanding why the condensation is there. We regularly find blocked eaves, poor airflow and insulation fitted in a way that stops the roof breathing. Adding vents without looking at the whole roof doesn't always solve it, so we investigate the cause and recommend what will.

A Recent Job

A house with non-breathable bitumen sarking felt had heavy condensation in the roof space because there wasn't enough airflow. We fitted a new dry ridge ventilation system and internal lap vents. Within 2 to 3 days of finishing, the condensation had cleared, with no need for a new roof.

Signs of a Ventilation Problem

  • Condensation in the roof space
  • Too much moisture, or mould, in the loft
  • Stale air with no airflow through the roof
  • Black bitumen felt under the tiles, which does not breathe

How Long It Takes

Usually 1 to 2 working days, depending on the size of the property and the roof structure.
